question:
pp-selectid (Protocol Pulse clip-video builder), the build driver's RULING 107 (1) guard (tests/package/proof_ledger.py, uncommitted). THE GUARD: a build whose inputs fingerprint the same as an earlier FINISHED build that left NOTHING undone (open_work(...) == 0) is skipped as "NOTHING NEW" (no model asked, $0). THE FINDING (the independent verifier, Nov 23): its offline drill measured no word check at all (every download blocked), recorded "0 items left undone", and the identical re-run was refused as NOTHING NEW; a real build whose downloads failed would have its next identical build skipped the same way. THE CHANGE: open_work now also counts, in the clean pass's prescreen record AND in the never-empty pass's (res["never_empty"]["soft_record"]["prescreen"]), every moment whose "second_pass" (L-v 2), "hook_onset" (G17a) or "trim_cut" entry starts "NOT MEASURED" (the exact prefix package._build writes for a check that could not run; a measured failure reads "L-v 2 FAIL" / "FAIL: ..." / "not cuttable ..."), each (check, moment) once.
CHECK, quoting the code: can a build with an unmeasured check still be followed by a NOTHING NEW skip; can a measured failure or a pass now count as undone (so the guard never skips, or a skip loops); can a missing or malformed record raise here. Report only what the code shows.

consensus_findings.issue: The new unmeasured scan can raise on a malformed record: it calls .items() on the value retrieved for second_pass/hook_onset/trim_cut after only an `or {}` fallback, so a non-empty non-dict value (or a non-dict prescreen object) causes AttributeError instead of being treated as undone or skipped.
consensus_findings.evidence: for mid, v in ((p or {}).get(k) or {}).items() if str(v).startswith("NOT MEASURED")
consensus_findings.fix: Guard with isinstance before calling .get/.items, e.g. `p = p if isinstance(p, dict) else {}` and `container = p.get(k); if not isinstance(container, dict): continue`.

consensus_findings.issue: Undefined variable 'pre' used in set comprehension
consensus_findings.evidence:
unmeasured = {(k, mid) for p in (pre, soft_pre) for k in ("second_pass", "hook_onset", "trim_cut")   # the verifier,
                  for mid, v in ((p or {}).get(k) or {}).items() if str(v).startswith("NOT MEASURED"))
consensus_findings.fix: Define 'pre' before use or remove it from the tuple, e.g., use (soft_pre,) instead of (pre, soft_pre).

consensus_findings.issue: Undefined variable 'pre' used in set comprehension will cause a NameError.
consensus_findings.evidence: unmeasured = {(k, mid) for p in (pre, soft_pre) for k in ("second_pass", "hook_onset", "trim_cut")
consensus_findings.fix: Define 'pre' before its use in the set comprehension, likely as the primary prescreen record from the result object: pre = (res or {}).get("prescreen") or {}

missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.issue: The new `soft_pre` extraction can also raise AttributeError on malformed records: `or {}` only replaces falsy values, so a truthy non-dict `res`, `never_empty`, or `soft_record` will fail on `.get`.
missed_in_cycle2_unvoted.fix: Use isinstance checks or a safe dict accessor before calling `.get`, e.g. only call `.get` when the value is a dict, otherwise substitute {}.
Define 'h' or pass it as an argument to the open_work function.
